argument_macro_structure.dominant_argument_form: Dialectical refutation with counterexample and analogical reasoning
argument_macro_structure.premise_explicitness: Partially explicit; Searle's argument is given as numbered premises, but author's replies are often implicit and reconstructed

argumentative_quality.dialectical_reasonableness: High: author concedes Searle's argument is logical and grants partial points before replying
argumentative_quality.logical_relevance: All objections and replies target the reference-fixing vs reference-functioning distinction
argumentative_quality.premise_acceptability: Relies on intuitions about baptism, direct reference, and statistical causation; some premises are controversial

distinctions_drawn: Fixing reference vs functioning through a description
Unique descriptive content vs meaningful descriptive content
Object as causal/explanatory factor vs descriptive content as correlated factor
explicit_definitions_given: Rigid designator: a term that directly refers to the same object in all possible worlds
Baptism: the initial fixing of a proper name's referent
Descriptive content: properties or descriptions that uniquely pick out an object

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: Author anticipates three Searlean objections: (1) revised baptism objection, (2) ostension objection, (3) inherent descriptive content objection; each is answered
objections_raised: Searle's initial argument: baptism requires descriptive content, so Kripke is descriptivist
Searle's revised argument: even if names later rigidly designate, the baptism itself is descriptivist
Searle's ostension objection: baptism by pointing still involves descriptive content
Searle's inherent-content objection: names like 'Katie' carry descriptive content (gender tone)

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Thought experiments, counterexamples, analogical reasoning, statistical analogy

philosophical_orientation.grounding: Analytic philosophy of language; Kripkean direct reference theory
philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: Proper names, rigid designation, reference fixing, descriptivism

structural_organization.structure_type: Dialectical: thesis, exposition, objection, reply, revised objection, counterexample, further replies, conclusion

summary_of_core_decisions: The paper's core move is to separate the causal/explanatory role of the object from the merely practical role of descriptive content at baptism. The hospital mix-up case is intended to show that a baptism can succeed even when the descriptive content is false, so the object, not the description, is the real referent-fixer.

thesis_commitment.conclusion_type: Negative thesis: Kripke's theory is not descriptivist
thesis_commitment.hedging_density_in_final_paragraph: Low: final conclusion is assertive and unqualified
